hook: This Cold Drink Might Trigger Your Prostate
claim: Prostadine is a liquid dropper supplement sold to support a healthy prostate, kidneys and urinary tract. It contains nine ingredients, most of them seaweeds.
story: Four of the nine ingredients are iodine-rich seaweeds (nori, wakame, kelp and bladderwrack), with iodine added separately as well. The sales page cites studies on iodine and prostate cancer, but iodine supplements are not a recognized prostate treatment.
ing_note: Amounts aren't disclosed, so the total iodine dose from four seaweeds plus added iodine is unknown.
use: Two full droppers (2 ml) a day, preferably in the morning, according to the website.
price_note: Prostadine is sold as 2 bottles (+$9.99 shipping), 2+1 bottles or 3+3 bottles with free shipping; totals appear on the order page.
checks: Saw palmetto did no better than placebo for urinary symptoms in the largest trials (STEP, CAMUS).
Large amounts of iodine can trigger thyroid problems, especially in older adults with existing thyroid nodules.
Shilajit products have been found contaminated with heavy metals when not purified.
The 'cold drink' headline is a curiosity hook; there's no evidence a cold drink 'triggers' the prostate.
cons: Main prostate ingredient failed in large trials
verdict: Prostadine is essentially a seaweed and iodine tonic with saw palmetto. The iodine is a real concern for anyone with thyroid disease, and the prostate evidence is weak. Men with urinary symptoms should see a doctor; BPH has effective, well-tested treatments, and a PSA test helps rule out cancer.
